title: Global sections of the constructed increasing-tuple sheaf complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$ any morphism of schemes, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ any finite family, and $G$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module. The global-section complex of $f_*(\operatorname{extend} C(U,G))$ [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction] is isomorphic as an integer cochain complex of $A$-modules to the extension of the increasing-tuple section complex [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], with scalars restricted along $A\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ induced by $f$. No affineness, quasi-coherence or covering hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 01FM, 02KG and 02KH; termwise sheaf and affine comparison before cohomology

proof.text:
The intersection presheaf V ↦ G(V ∩ W) is already a sheaf: it is the direct
image from the over site of W. Its sheafification unit is therefore an isomorphism.
Module sheafification is additive and preserves finite biproducts, hence finite products. The forgetful functor and evaluation preserve products. Therefore the degree-p global sections of the sheafified product are the product of G(W_t). At the top open, top ∩ W_t = W_t.
Pushforward sections at the top are sections on X, and restriction of scalars is
along A → Γ(X,O_X), the composite of ΓSpecIso.inv and f.appTop. These identifications
commute with each face restriction since they are the sheafification unit followed
by restriction along top ∩ W_t = W_t. Additivity then identifies the finite signed
sums defining both differentials. Thus the degree comparisons form a complex
isomorphism. In negative degrees both extended complexes are zero, and the unique
maps give the comparison there. The empty family and empty tuple types contribute
zero modules, and require no covering or affineness hypothesis.
